notes: Reviewer ran in single_context (single Claude Code instance); reviewer_independent_candidates.txt was written to disk (454 lines, 426 candidates) BEFORE agent1_output.json was opened in order to preserve unbiased candidate derivation. Overall the Extractor performed competently on the major flagship entities of the paper (MERFISH+, Stereo-seq, MSN subtypes, GP neuron subtypes, astrocyte/oligodendrocyte subtypes, the DL-VM gradient, striosome-matrix architecture, all the canonical genes DRD1/DRD2/PDYN/etc.) and ran a proper 4-round masking loop with explicit unmasked_candidates lists per round terminating zero-delta. Surface forms are literal (no regex), the coreference pass was performed (49.9% of entities have indirect_references with referring_phrase records), and the JSON conforms to schema. The Ontology Mapper correctly recalled standard IDs for the spot-checked entries (HGNC, UBERON, CHEBI, GO, NCBITaxon, RRID, CL) and confidence levels are appropriate. The triggered re-extraction is targeted: ~24 missed entities (primarily Figure S5 non-neuronal cell types, Figure S9 region-enriched genes, the paper-defining 'spatial transcriptomics' concept, several diseases mentioned in references and Discussion, a few methods/reagents). Mapping coverage at 59.9% is below the 80% PASS threshold; ~48 of the 164 unmapped are legitimately unmappable (paper-specific Allen-taxonomy cluster names and commercial vendors) and the remainder are real ontology-mapping gaps for Methods, Algorithms, Software, Reagents, and Diseases. Recommendation: invoke a targeted-addition Extractor pass, then a final Mapper pass to lift coverage; the existing entities and masking artifacts can be retained without modification.
